  STAFF REPORT
  AGENDA ITEM NO. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  James Markel, Recreation Supervisor
Date:  August 17, 2022

Subject:  Annual Sports and Aquatics Division Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Youth Sports:
Summer & Fall 2021 were still under strict covid guidelines which prohibited our ability
to offer any youth sports classes.
Youth Sports resumed during the Winter 2021 session. Due to covid guidelines our
traditional 9-week classes were held outdoors. The following classes were conducted:
Basketball Fundamentals (2 classes, ages 5-12), Volleyball Fundamentals (1 class,
ages 10-17), Baseball Fundamentals (3 classes, ages 3-12) and Multi-Sport (3 classes,
ages 3-12). Class sizes were reduced to ensure all covid guidelines were met and
enrollment across all fundamental classes totaled 100 participants.
Spring 2022 continued with the traditional 9-week session with all programming
resuming to normal operations. Our team of Recreation leaders developed a new Multi-
Sport class which included a different combination of sports such as soccer, football &
tennis. Basketball and volleyball classes returned indoors and our contract classes
were able to resume instruction as well. Soccer Fundamentals held at GOALS had a
total of 6 classes, Karate restarted their monthly classes and tennis resumed with Level
1 and 2 lessons. We had a total of 400 participants in our youth sports classes during
the Spring. In April 2022, we hosted our first ever Jr. NBA Challenge. The Challenge
provided boys and girls, ages 13 and younger, the opportunity to showcase their
basketball abilities through a dribbling, shooting, and rebounding skills competition. Each
of our participants completed the challenge, had their photo taken, and were provided with
a certificate of completion.

  4
 Summer 2022 classes are currently halfway through, and participants’ feedback has
been extremely positive. We have expanded programming again and have added
another Baseball Fundamental class that takes place on Friday evenings at Legacy
High School. Staff continues to work hard creating new lesson plans and finding
alternative ways to engage the participants. At the culmination of each 9-week class,
participants celebrate with a scrimmage, potluck, and award ceremony. The following
classes are currently taking place: Basketball Fundamentals (3 classes), Volleyball
Fundamentals (1 class), Multi-Sport Pass, Serve, Score (2 classes), Baseball
Fundamentals (3 classes), Multi-Sport Shoot, Kick, Hit (3 classes), and Baseball
Fundamentals at Legacy HS (3 classes). Our contract classes (Soccer, Karate, and
Tennis) also reached class capacity. In total across all youth sport classes we had 450
participants register during the Summer session.

Adult Sports:
Summer 2021 kicked off with a new event, Ballin’ After Dark. Teams of 5 played pick-
up basketball rules, called their own fouls, and competed in a tournament style format
for prizes. Games were up to 11 points with staff as official scorekeepers and to
provide final call on all judgement plays. We had a second “B.A.D.” event in August and
had 12 registered teams. The events had great energy from the participants and
spectators and were welcomed with great appreciation and satisfaction.
Winter/Spring 2021 brought back our much-anticipated Men’s and Co-ed Softball
Leagues. For many of the teams this was their first time back on the softball diamond
since the onset of the pandemic back in March of 2020. Players were embracing each
other on opposite teams and discussing how they hadn’t seen one another since the
pandemic. Our Men’s League played on Thursday evenings and began with 1 division
of 8 teams. Our Co-ed League played on Friday evenings, and they started with 2
divisions of 6 teams. Winners in their respective division won a team trophy along with
each player receiving a Dri-Fit performance t-shirt donning the South Gate Champion
title. Second place winners received an aluminum water bottle with City of South Gate
Adult Softball artwork.
Summer 2022 is currently hosting both the Men’s and Co-ed Softball Leagues. We did
see an increase in both leagues and continue to receive daily inquiries about the next
season. Currently, our Thursday Men’s league has 2 divisions, with a total of 13 teams,
while our Friday Co-ed League has 2 divisions of 8 teams for a total of 16 teams.
Winners of the current season are set to receive Softball Champion tank tops; second
place will receive a different style of aluminum water bottle with updated artwork. In
addition to the Adult Softball Leagues, our Friday Night Men’s Basketball League has
also returned.  Currently we have 6 teams competing for the Summer 2022
Championship title and to have their team’s name hung in the rafters of the Sports
Center gymnasium.

  5
 Fitness
The Sports Center redesigned the membership program in July 2021, which introduced
more convenient options for our members. Members now have the option to include
access to the Swim Stadium by purchasing the Splash Add-on to an individual monthly
membership. Splash add-ons can be cancelled by members as they please without
having to cancel their Sports or Fitness memberships.
Memberships steadily increased every quarter and continued to get closer to pre-
pandemic levels as the year progressed. Although the Personal Training program did
not restart until 2022, it was greeted with excitement from current/new members and
saw the same steady success as memberships throughout the year.
We conducted an Open House event in January 2022. The event was free to attend
and highlighted the Sports Center facility and its programming. We offered condensed
versions of Group Exercise Classes, Personal Training assessments, and fun sports
activities. Attendees also had the opportunity to receive a Subway lunch by
participating in activities throughout the day.
The Fitness division increased its Youth programming by adding the first Youth group
exercise class, Young & Fit, to the classes offered in the membership program. The
class runs concurrently with our Boot Camp to allow parents and children the option to
workout in the same vicinity, while having individualized workouts and instructors.
Our inaugural Fun Run recently took place on July 16, 2022. The event was $10 and
included a t-shirt, tote bag, and vouchers from local vendors. The Fun Run consisted of
a one mile run within the park, filled with inflatable obstacles and water slides,
sprinklers, slime, and mud zones. There were approximately 600 registered runners,
we also had vendors, a DJ, and many spectators. The event culminated in a raffle of
various prizes donated from our generous supporters and donors.

Aquatics

In the summer of 2021, all COVID restrictions for Aquatics were lifted as it was deemed
a low-risk activity. The Aquatics division became fully operational, offering several
organized programs as well as recreational activities for everyone. The Patricia G.
Mitchell Swim Stadium was open 7 days a week for Lap, Adult, and Family Swim with
approximately 14,000 paid daily admissions. We also launched our Splash membership
program to great success, with about 1,000 reoccurring memberships. Group, Private
and Semi-Private swim lessons for all ages, runs spring-fall and was at capacity every
month. We registered 4,600 total youth and 400 adult lesson participants throughout
the year.

The Swim Stadium also offered several therapy and fitness classes for adults/seniors,
such as: SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim, and Open Play Water Polo. We
featured specialized and aquatic sports programs like Gators Swim Academy, Junior
Water Polo, Pre-Comp, Surfing 101, as well as hosting competitive swim team/partner

  6
 organization South Gate Aquatics Club year-round. The Swim Stadium is also host to
several other local swim teams throughout the year. March 2022, in partnership with
SGAC and in celebration of the Azalea Festival, we hosted our first swim meet since the
pandemic began. This event served as a fundraiser for the swim team and brought in 5
local teams with over 100 local swimmers.

May is designated as National Water Safety Month, so the Swim Stadium in partnership
with the Parks & Rec Social Media Team campaigned all month long to bring water
safety awareness to the community. We celebrated International Water Safety Day on
May 15 with our 3 annual Water Safety Bash which brought in over 100 participants. We
had our first ever Community Swim Day on June 19 celebrating Summer Kick-Off. The
event featured music, lawn games, first aid and water safety demo booths, plus Family
Swim. On June 24 we joined thousands of aquatics facilities all over the world for the
World’s Largest Swim Lesson with almost 100 participants. All events were free to the
community and sponsored by our partner organization South Gate Aquatics Club.

The Swim Stadium is available for rentals year-round and was pretty much booked
spring through fall. Once again, the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Statium hosted the South
Central Swim League, which puts on about 6 meets throughout the year. These meets
usually bring in over 500 local competitive swimmers with over 1,000 spectators and are
a major highlight of the year. Another major highlight is the LA84 program, which
through their generous grant of almost $18K, allowed us to provide almost 700 youth
ages 7-17 with free swimming lessons.

As first responders, Aquatics Staff is consistently training, and in June 2022 held our
annual recertification course certifying about 50 Lifeguards in American Red Cross
Lifeguarding with CPR/AED For Professional Rescuers, First Aid, Administering
Emergency Oxygen and Bloodborne Pathogens Training. We also offered a Lifeguard
Class with 10 participants, from which we plan to hire additional Aquatics Staff.

  STAFF REPORT
  AGENDA ITEM NO. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  August 15, 2022

Subject:  Update on Parks & Recreation Department Major Projects

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file

Report Summary: The Parks & Recreation Department maintains over 185 acres of
landscape and numerous community centers and support facilities throughout the City.
These parks and facilities require continual maintenance and at times major capital
improvement projects must be scheduled to keep areas safe for the public. Below is a
list of current projects slated for the Department and where they are in the process:

Auditorium Roof Project
The auditorium roof has had issues with leaking for several years and our Public Works
Department has worked diligently to provide patching. This process is no longer viable
and there is a need for a total replacement of the roof. We have secured some funding
for the project, but with costs escalating we will need additional resources. Also, if we
replace the roof, we should replace the A/C units on the roof to meet code.
Estimated cost:  $900,000
Current funding:  $400,000 (Approx.)

Boy Scout Huts
There are 8 buildings in the Boy Scout Hut area. Many have not had any renovations
since the 70’s. There are several areas of concern, the most pressing of which is the
roofs of several of the buildings. Funding was originally secured through CDBG but our
HUD representative determined that the huts were not eligible.
Estimated cost:  $1,000,000
Current funding:  None

Cesar Chavez Playground
Located near Santa Fe and Southern Avenues this playground needs total renovation.
Staff contacted the original vendor and obtained estimates for replacements. Plans are
in process and completion should be in September.

  8
 Estimated cost:  $150,000
Current funding:  $150,000

Circle Park
Concepts are for a total renovation of the site to include new basketball courts, a
playground, and parking. Plans have been completed and are under review by SCE.
Construction may start as early as December 2022.
Estimated cost:  $5.8 million
Current funding:  $5.8 million

Hollydale Community Park
Plans are complete, RFP for contractors has been released and plans are to start the
project in October 2022. This will be a total renovation of the park and will include a
new community center, as well as a playground, and basketball courts.
Estimated cost:  $4.15 million
Current funding:  $4.15 million

New Community Center (GCH)
Planning process started in 2019 but Covid cut short the process. Replacement of the
Girls Clubhouse with a new three-story building will need to wait until financing is
available.
Estimated cost:  $21 million
Current funding:  None

Park Yard Roof Project
This project included replacement of the roof at the Park Maintenance Yard and over
the parking bays for equipment. Project was completed in May 2022.
Estimated cost:  $100,000
Current funding:  $100,000

South Gate Park Fence Project
This project to replace the different fences throughout South Gate Park started in 2016
and has been funded and lost its funding on two different occasions. Currently we have
updated the plans and will be going out to bid in October or November.
Estimated cost:  $850,000
Current funding:  $850,000

Sports Center PA System
A new system that will allow staff to provide announcements and information to the
public on a regular basis.
Estimated cost:  $82,000
Current funding:  $72,000

Urban Orchard
New 7-acre park located between the 710 freeway and the LA River. Currently under
construction with an estimated completion date of January 2023.
Estimated cost:  $30+ million
Current funding:  $30+ million

  STAFF REPORT
  AGENDA ITEM NO. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  August 16, 2022
Subject:  Recreation 4th Quarter FY 2021/22 Review

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: The following report will cover recreation programming that took place
between April-June. During the 4th quarter of the year the department increased programming
opportunities based on the reduction of COVID-19 guidelines. Although, we are not near our
normal operation, the results over the past three months are very encouraging.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
Two of our partner organizations have started back up. AYSO has not started back up, we are
in communication with them and hoping to start soon.
South Gate Aztecs (Youth Football & Cheer): Monday – Friday (5:00pm-8:00pm) & Saturday’s
(9:00am-12:00pm) at Hollydale Regional Park
SGJAA: Conducted 2022 Spring Baseball and Softball Seasons. Basketball registrations and
preparation for season currently taking place.

Fitness Center
Our 4th quarter saw a small increase in memberships. We had about 18,000 membership
check-ins and sold 1,943 memberships for the quarter. However, with the rise in memberships,
we conversely see a decrease in daily admissions sold at approximately 6,500 for this quarter.

Personal Training hours have been steady at 172 and there seems to be an increase in Private
trainings over the Semi-private options.

We concluded our Winter Biggest Loser, which is always very successful and began preparing
for our Youth Biggest Loser which was set to debut in the summer.

Registration for all Youth Classes was slightly better than expected and there seems to be a
growing demand for youth fitness.

Youth Sports:
  • Baseball Fundamentals (3 classes – total of 60 participants)
  • Basketball Fundamentals (3 classes – total of 55 participants)
  • Traditionnel Multisport (3 classes – total of 61 participants)
  • NEW Multi-Sport (2 classes – total of 30 kids)

  10
   •  Soccer Fundamentals (6 classes – total of 100 participants)
  •  Tennis (3 classes – total of 20 participants)
  •  Volleyball (1 class – total of 20 participants)
  •  Karate has resumed with regular classes

Special Events
  • Our Jr. NBA Skills Challenge provided boys and girls, ages 13 and younger, the opportunity
  to showcase their basketball talents through a dribbling, shooting, and rebounding skills
  competition. Each of our participants completed the challenge, had their photo taken, and
  were provided a certificate of completion.

Adult Sports:
Men’s Softball
  • Summer Season begun with 2 divisions on Thursday evenings and a total of 13 teams.
Co-ed Softball
  • Summer Season begun with 2 divisions on Friday evenings and a total of 16 teams.
Men’s Basketball League
  • This if the first season back since the pandemic, the summer season has 1 division of 6
  teams.
Open Play Volleyball
  • There were 650 daily passes sold
Special Events
  • Over the Line Baseball Tourney is currently taking registration

Aquatics
  • The Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium was in full bloom during the 4th quarter. It was
  open 7 days a week with various sessions throughout the day. We offered
  Adult/Lap/Family Swim Sessions, totaling over 7,997 paid daily admissions. Our Splash
  membership program saw an uptick in numbers, with almost 2,000 new enrollees. The
  Learn-to-Swim program, 6 months & over, was full every month, with about 1,580
  registrations. All Youth & Adult Swim Lessons, including private and semiprivate, had
  500 registrations. Aquatic Fitness programs, (SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim,
  and Water Polo Open Play) saw an increase in participation.
  • The Swim Stadium hosted a number of special events, including a Water Safety Bash on
  May 1, celebrating International Water Safety Day with almost 100 participants
  • Joined thousands of aquatics facilities all over the world for the World’s Largest Swim
  Lesson on June 24 with almost 100 participants
  • Had our first Community Swim Day on June 19 celebrating Summer Kick-Off and
  featuring music, lawn games, first aid, and water safety demo booths, plus Family Swim.
  All events were free to the community and sponsored by our partner organization South
  Gate Aquatics Club.
  • In June we also introduced new programs, Junior Water Polo, Gators Swim Academy,
  and Surfing 101.
  • We’ve been consistently booked for weekend rentals for private events since early
  spring.
  • Once again, we are hosting the South-Central Swim League with 2 meets during this
  season and 2 more in the late summer. These meets usually bring in over 500 local
  competitive swimmers and over 1,000 spectators
  • A major highlight of the year is the LA84 program, which through their generous grant of
  almost $18K, allowed us to provide almost 700 youth, ages 7-17, with free swimming
  lessons.

  11
   •  In June we held our annual recertification course certifying about 50 Lifeguards in
  American Red Cross Lifeguarding with CPR/AED For Professional Rescuers, First Aid,
  Administering Emergency Oxygen and Bloodborne Pathogens Training. We also offered
  a Lifeguard Class with 10 participants

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 3,020. In the last quarter we had 14 posts, 251 stories, 3 reels
and 1 video. Community engagement has been positive, and patrons are utilizing direct
messages to ask questions and seek information

Contract Classes
All classes have returned to full schedule. Dance, Tumbling, Music (piano/guitar), & Art Classes
were full to capacity. We added a few extra Baby Boogie, Tiny Tumblers, and Baby Ballet
Classes since they are the most popular. There were also Cultural Arts workshops offered on
Saturdays. Unfortunately, some of those had to be canceled due to low enrollment but staff is
reevaluating on how to entice the community to attend, such as making craft projects at
Concerts in Park.
The Tot Time and Tiny 2s started in Spring and Tiny 2’s filled the registration fast. Staff will add
another class in Fall.

Special Events
Easter Festival was conducted for the first time, since the pandemic, on site and at the Golf
Course. All participants were greeted by the Bunny and were able to play carnival games and
do crafts. The Egg Hunts are the most popular and finding the golden egg is very competitive.
There were 130 in attendance and the kids really enjoyed themselves.

  STAFF REPORT
  AGENDA ITEM NO. 4
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  August 15, 2022

Subject:  Grounds and Facility Maintenance 4th Quarter Report

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance

  ➢ During the fourth quarter we maintained 10 baseball fields – prepared, dragged,
  packed, and watered five days a week. Light grading was performed on the large
  quad, diamonds 1-4.

  ➢ Staff has pressure washed picnic tables, benches, playground areas, handball
  courts, small quad, bandstand, outside restrooms, Golf Course, Senior Center, City
  Hall and other areas as needed, and in preparation for rentals.

  ➢ Grounds staff have replaced over 350 sprinklers throughout Hollydale Regional,
  South Gate, and Cesar Chavez Parks during this quarter.

  ➢ Continuing to pressure wash and disinfecting playgrounds and Dog and Skate
  parks, including other open areas. Grounds staff continues servicing and
  beautifying over 180 acres of Park land.

Park Facility Maintenance

  ➢ Addressing the ongoing challenges of restroom cleanliness staff continues using a
  weekly restroom disinfecting program to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and other
  germs using a C3 Disinfecting Machine to apply disinfectants and cleaners. Once
  the product is sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure
  thoroughness.

  ➢ With the anticipated high use of our parks during spring and summer we have

  13
   implemented a third daily restroom service to our outdoor restrooms.

➢ We have continued the implemented use of “Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment”
  for more coverage in our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and
  outdoor restroom facilities, along with a pressure washing program. These
  disinfecting and cleaning tools will allow us to use them simultaneously, giving us
  more overall coverage. Set ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables,
  chairs, door handles, and a/v equipment.

➢ We purchased a new pressure washer for more efficiency in our disinfecting efforts.

➢ The installation of ADA doors in all our South Gate Park public buildings has been
  completed

➢ Due to current COVID-19 restrictions being relaxed we have been in full operation
  with Department classes returning, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports, and
  clubs returning. We continued to host several COVID-19 vaccine clinics, testing,
  blood drives and food giveaways for the community during this period.

➢ The Community Service Worker program is also back to full operation going back to
  are original limited intake of (15) people maximum per day staff for safety.

Staff continues to work hard to keep our parks clean and safe. As we move forward this
year and facility programming reopens, staff will create a plan to service indoor and
outdoor facilities accordingly.

  STAFF REPORT
  AGENDA ITEM NO. 7
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  August 25, 2022

Subject:  Report on Activities for Halloween

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary: Per Commissioner Cypert’s request staff is listing the activities
being offered this year at the Halloween Haunt. Because Hollydale Community Park is
closed due to upgrades, staff anticipates a higher volume of people this year. Keeping
that in mind, staff will not have jumpers. But there will still be something for everyone to
enjoy!

The Halloween Haunt will take place at the large quad (behind the Senior Center) and
from 6:00pm to 9:00pm. We will have a variety of carnival games, approximately 25,
where each participant, win or lose, will receive candy. We also have the Halloween
costume contests for all age groups in different categories and each winner will receive
a goodie bag filled with candy and other treats!

For anyone looking for a good fright there will be a haunted maze, for the younger
children there’s a mini train ride, and of course the ever-popular picture booth. Also,
staff is looking to secure a hay ride, which has been enjoyed by all in the past.
